source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Overview of institutions relevant to Cambodia's mango export sector, per the GIZ/SRECA guideline (December 2020 edition).

Policy and regulatory bodies: MAFF's General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) is the lead technical authority for orchard/farm registration, phytosanitary inspection, and coordination with China's GACC on the bilateral protocol.

Research and training support: the guideline names the Royal University of Agriculture (RUA) as playing a role in mango research, technical training, and capacity-building for growers and exporters — the source describes USAID/USDA-linked technical assistance channelled partly through RUA to strengthen agribusiness and food-safety capacity for export-oriented crops including mango.

Financial/tax incentives: Cambodia's Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) has issued sub-decrees relevant to agro-processing exporters, including Sub-Decree No. 124 on tax incentives for SMEs in priority sectors (dated around October 2018) and Sub-Decree No. 50 on customs incentives for SMEs (dated around March 2019). Exporters and processors, including smaller agro-enterprises, may be able to access these incentives — current eligibility and application procedures should be confirmed directly with MEF or GDA.

China-side trade promotion contacts and events: see the companion marketing/trade-fair file (mango_export_marketing_and_trade_promotion) for specific fairs and websites relevant to connecting with Chinese buyers.
caveat: This document is very likely the same GIZ/SRECA fresh-mango-export-to-China guideline series already represented as mango Source C in the knowledge base (processed in Batch 43), but this is a later, more complete edition (dated December 2020, 67pp, vs. the earlier-processed 53pp version with data through 2018). Some content below (market/policy context, registration procedures, marketing section) is likely NEW relative to Source C; other content (GACC protocol, phytosanitary basics, documentation) likely OVERLAPS with Source C. This has not been reconciled against Source C's actual files — a duplicate-check comparing this source (tagged G) against Source C is recommended before both are considered final. Institutional/contacts overview; likely partially new relative to Source C's market-access/contacts file, which per the prior handover focused more on HS codes, payment terms, and a direct contact list rather than institutional actors like RUA/MEF.
